newsitem.title: ITALY: SOCCER-HISTORIC UEFA CUP WIN FOR SCHALKE.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-HISTORIC UEFA CUP WIN FOR SCHALKE.

text.p: Germany's Schalke beat Internazionale Milan on penalties in the second leg of the UEFA Cup final on Wednesday to capture their first European club trophy in 93 years.

The visitors, 1-0 ahead from the first leg, won 4-1 in a penalty shoot-out after the two sides, with Inter down to 10 men after Salvatore Fresi was sent off in the 90th minute, were locked 1-1 on aggregate after extra time.

Chilean Ivan Zamorano had saved Inter when they were six minutes from defeat in normal time with a right-footed flick into the net after England midfielder Paul Ince headed on a cross from Alessandro Pistone.
The crowd erupted with relief after 84 minutes of often subdued anguish.
After Fresi was sent off, Inter played with more purpose and went close to scoring on several occasions. But Schalke, whose last trophy was the German Cup in 1972, kept their nerve.

Inter's hopes of a third UEFA Cup win in a decade evaporated in the penalty shoot-out when goalkeeper Jens Lehmann saved Zamorano's opening shot with a dive to the right and then Dutch substitute Aron Winter sidefooted his spot-kick wide of the goal.
